title: Laravel MVP: From Idea to Launch in 4-12 Weeks (2026 Guide)
meta_description: Build and launch a Laravel MVP in 4-12 weeks in 2026. Get the complete sprint framework, pre-built architecture decisions, and validation strategies used by successful SaaS founders.
excerpt: Most software MVPs fail not because of bad code, but because of over-engineering. Laravel's opinionated ecosystem makes it the ideal framework for validating ideas fast—without sacrificing code quality. This guide gives you the exact 12-week sprint plan, architectural shortcuts, and go-live checklist used by successful SaaS founders.
author: Professional Content Team

content_structure.introduction: Hook: 42% of startups fail building things nobody wants. Define the lean MVP philosophy applied to Laravel. Preview: scope definition, tech stack, 12-week sprint plan, post-launch strategy.
content_structure.section_1: Scope definition: user story prioritization, MoSCoW method (Must/Should/Could/Won't), the 3 questions to cut features (Does it validate the hypothesis? Can users pay without it? Can we add it later?).
content_structure.section_2: Tech stack choices: Laravel 12 + Livewire v3 vs. Inertia.js + Vue/React, Filament for admin, Cashier for billing, Breeze for auth. Decision guide for each choice.
content_structure.section_3: Sprints 1-4: project setup, authentication (Breeze/Jetstream), core data models, database schema, basic UI, deployment pipeline (Laravel Forge + DigitalOcean).
content_structure.section_4: Sprints 5-8: core feature development, billing integration (Cashier + Stripe), email notifications, basic analytics, user onboarding flow.
content_structure.section_5: Sprints 9-12: Pest test suite, performance optimization, SEO basics, security hardening, go-live checklist (SSL, backups, monitoring, error tracking).
content_structure.conclusion: The 12-week MVP calendar with milestones. CTA: Download the Laravel MVP Sprint Plan Template.

title: Serverless Laravel 2026: Vapor vs FrankenPHP Performance Guide
meta_description: Compare Laravel Vapor vs FrankenPHP for serverless performance in 2026. Benchmarks, cost analysis, and deployment guides to choose the right runtime for your Laravel app.
excerpt: Serverless Laravel has matured dramatically—you can now run production Laravel applications with sub-50ms cold starts, zero server management, and infrastructure that scales from 0 to 100,000 requests automatically. This guide benchmarks Laravel Vapor against FrankenPHP and gives you the deployment playbook for both.
author: Professional Content Team

content_structure.introduction: Hook: sub-250ms cold starts, zero server management. Define serverless in the Laravel context. Preview: Vapor deep-dive, FrankenPHP explainer, benchmarks, cost analysis, decision framework.
content_structure.section_1: Serverless for Laravel: what runs on Lambda (HTTP workers), what doesn't (long-running queues need workarounds), cold start strategies, asset management via CloudFront.
content_structure.section_2: Laravel Vapor: deployment flow, environment management, database/cache/queue setup on AWS (RDS, ElastiCache, SQS), cost breakdown, limitations (file system, long jobs).
content_structure.section_3: FrankenPHP: Caddy-based PHP server, early hints, worker mode (Laravel Octane compatible), HTTP/3 support, Docker-based deployment, performance profile.
content_structure.section_4: Benchmark table: throughput (req/s), p50/p95/p99 latency, memory usage, cold start time. Tested on identical workloads: Vapor, FrankenPHP on Fly.io, Octane on Forge VPS.
content_structure.section_5: Cost analysis: Vapor costs at 1M/10M/100M monthly requests vs. FrankenPHP on Fly.io or Render.com vs. traditional Forge VPS. Break-even calculator reference.
content_structure.conclusion: Decision flowchart: use Vapor if (team prefers AWS, need true scale-to-zero); FrankenPHP if (need maximum raw throughput, containerized deployment). CTA: Download the Serverless Laravel Deployment Checklist.
